questions.stem_latex:
Preeti deposits \$300 into a savings account on 1 January 2024. The account accrues interest at the rate of $3.6\%$ p.a. compounding monthly. Preeti plans to deposit \$300 at the start of every month thereafter until the end of 2029.

Let $A_n$ be the amount that Preeti has in her account at the end of the $n$th month (where the 1$^{\text{st}}$ month is January 2024).

Calculate the value of Preeti’s account at the end of 2029, and find how much more money she would have had if she hadn’t gone to university.

solutions.latex:
The areas are equal, so when integrating from 0 to $k$, the area below the $x$-axis will cancel out the area above the $x$-axis:

$$\begin{aligned}\int_0^k(x^2-1)\,dx&=0\\\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-x\right]_0^k&=0\\\dfrac{k^3}{3}-k&=0\\k^3-3k&=0\\k(k^2-3)&=0\\k&=0,\pm\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}$$

but $k>1$, $\therefore k=\sqrt{3}$

Alternative solution:

$$\begin{aligned}\left|\int_0^1(x^2-1)\,dx\right|&=\int_0^k(x^2-1)\,dx\\\left|\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-x\right]_0^1\right|&=\left[\dfrac{x^3}{3}-x\right]_1^k\\\left|\dfrac{1}{3}-1\right|&=\dfrac{k^3}{3}-k-\left(\dfrac{1}{3}-1\right)\\\dfrac{2}{3}&=\dfrac{k^3}{3}-k+\dfrac{2}{3}\end{aligned}$$

$\dfrac{k^3}{3}-k=0$ etc $\Rightarrow k=\sqrt{3}$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 3: Correct solution; 1st mark for writing a correct equation involving integrals; 2nd mark for integrating $x^2-1$; 3rd mark for finding the value of $k$. Note: you had to justify why $k$ is not 0 or $-\sqrt{3}$.

solutions.latex:
The arithmetic sequence is $1,\ 1+d,\ 1+2d,\ \ldots$

The geometric sequence is $1,\ r,\ r^2,\ \ldots$

Second terms are equal, so $r=1+d$

$14^{\text{th}}$ term of AS $=3$ times $3^{\text{rd}}$ term of GS, so $1+13d=r^2$

Solving simultaneously:

$$\begin{aligned}1+13d&=3(1+d)^2\\1+13d&=3+6d+3d^2\\3d^2-7d+2&=0\\(3d-1)(d-2)&=0\\d&=\dfrac{1}{3}\text{ or }2\end{aligned}$$

$d$ being $1/3$ would result in some terms of the arithmetic sequence not being integers (e.g. the second term would be $4/3$). Therefore $d=2$. Hence $r=1+2=3$
solutions.marks_breakdown: 4: Correct solution; 1st mark for correctly using one of the series formulas, e.g. obtaining $T_2=1+d$; 2nd mark for obtaining both equations connecting $r$ and $d$; 3rd mark for solving simultaneously to obtain the two values of $r$ or $d$.
